meta.description: High-signal AI voices curated for Lumina Signal

voices.name: Andrej Karpathy
voices.bio: Former Director of AI at Tesla and founding member of OpenAI. Creates the clearest from-scratch educational content on deep learning and LLMs.
voices.why: Best technical pedagogy currently available. Rare combination of frontier experience and teaching excellence.

voices.name: Dwarkesh Patel
voices.bio: Produces the most thoroughly prepared long-form interviews with frontier lab leaders and researchers.
voices.why: Exceptional depth, obsessive preparation, and unique access to decision-makers building frontier models.

voices.name: Yann LeCun
voices.bio: Turing Award winner. Leading voice on the limitations of pure scaling and advocate for open research and alternative architectures.
voices.why: One of the most influential long-term thinkers in the field with consistent, high-signal public positions.

voices.name: Demis Hassabis
voices.bio: Co-founder of DeepMind. Key figure in AGI research and scientific applications of AI (AlphaFold, etc.).
voices.why: Rare combination of scientific depth and leadership at the absolute frontier.

voices.name: Dario Amodei
voices.bio: CEO of Anthropic. Influential voice on scaling, safety, and responsible development of frontier models.
voices.why: High-signal public communications on both capabilities and risks from a frontier lab leader.

voices.name: swyx & Alessio Fanelli
voices.bio: The leading podcast for AI engineers. Covers agents, infrastructure, evals, and production systems with high technical density.
voices.why: Best ongoing coverage of real AI engineering practice.

voices.name: Arthur Mensch
voices.bio: CEO of Mistral AI. Leading European voice on open-weight models, sovereignty, and industrial AI strategy.
voices.why: Most important European voice at the frontier. Clear strategic thinking on open models and Europe’s position.

voices.name: Nathan Labenz
voices.bio: Deep conversations with builders and researchers focused on real model capabilities, evaluations, and practical strategy.
voices.why: Excellent signal on what models can actually do versus benchmarks.

voices.name: Yannic Kilcher
voices.bio: Produces rigorous, detailed walkthroughs of important machine learning papers.
voices.why: Highest-quality paper explanation content available publicly.

voices.name: AI Explained
voices.bio: Sober, careful analysis of new models, benchmarks, and claims in the AI space.
voices.why: Consistently low-hype, high-signal commentary on rapid developments.

voices.name: Nicolas Guyon
voices.bio: Leading French-language podcast on generative AI, with regular interviews of practitioners and experts.
voices.why: Best consistent high-signal French voice on practical and strategic AI topics.

voices.name: Ilya Sutskever
voices.bio: Former Chief Scientist of OpenAI. Deep technical and philosophical voice on the path to superintelligence.
voices.why: One of the most important technical minds in the field with rare public depth.

voices.name: Geoffrey Hinton
voices.bio: Pioneer of deep learning. Now focused on AI risk and the implications of advanced systems.
voices.why: Foundational contributions + increasingly important public voice on risks.

voices.name: Yoshua Bengio
voices.bio: Turing Award winner. Major voice on AI safety and responsible development.
voices.why: Deep technical credibility combined with strong safety advocacy.

voices.name: François Chollet
voices.bio: Creator of Keras. Influential thinker on the nature of intelligence and limitations of current approaches.
voices.why: Sharp, first-principles thinking on what intelligence actually requires.

voices.name: Thomas Wolf
voices.bio: Key figure in the open-source AI ecosystem through Hugging Face.
voices.why: Central voice for open models and the infrastructure around them.

voices.name: Jeremy Howard
voices.bio: Co-founder of fast.ai. Focused on making deep learning practical and accessible.
voices.why: Excellent practical teaching and strong opinions grounded in real usage.

voices.name: Simon Willison
voices.bio: Prolific experimenter and clear writer on practical applications of LLMs and AI tools.
voices.why: Extremely high signal-to-noise on what actually works in practice.

voices.name: 3Blue1Brown (Grant Sanderson)
voices.bio: Creates exceptional visual explanations of mathematical concepts underlying modern AI.
voices.why: Best mathematical intuition content for understanding the foundations of deep learning.

voices.name: Lex Fridman
voices.bio: Long-form conversations with leading scientists, engineers, and thinkers in AI and beyond.
voices.why: Broad reach and consistent access to important guests, even if less technically dense than specialized shows.

voices.name: Sarah Guo & Elad Gil
voices.bio: Podcast focused on AI startups, founders, and the business of frontier technology.
voices.why: Strong coverage of the company-building and investment side of AI.

voices.name: Stuart Russell
voices.bio: Author of the standard AI textbook. Leading voice on the control problem and value alignment.
voices.why: Foundational thinker on making AI systems provably beneficial.

voices.name: Ethan Mollick
voices.bio: Studies and writes about the real-world use of AI in work and education.
voices.why: Grounded, evidence-based perspective on how people actually use these tools.

voices.name: Hamel Husain
voices.bio: Focuses on production AI systems, evaluations, and practical workflows.
voices.why: High-signal content on the unsexy but critical parts of shipping AI products.

voices.name: Paul Christiano
voices.bio: One of the most influential thinkers on AI alignment and scalable oversight.
voices.why: Deep, careful reasoning on the hardest alignment problems.

voices.name: Neel Nanda
voices.bio: Leading public researcher and educator in mechanistic interpretability.
voices.why: Best public communication on how to actually understand model internals.

voices.name: Dan Hendrycks
voices.bio: Works on AI safety benchmarks, risk measurement, and policy-relevant research.
voices.why: Strong bridge between technical safety research and practical evaluation.

voices.name: Chris Olah
voices.bio: Pioneer of circuits-style interpretability and clear technical writing.
voices.why: Exceptional clarity and foundational work on understanding neural networks.

voices.name: Andrew Ng
voices.bio: Co-founder of Coursera and Google Brain. Major voice in AI education and practical adoption.
voices.why: Unmatched reach and clarity for educating the next generation of practitioners.

voices.name: Fei-Fei Li
voices.bio: Pioneer of ImageNet and leading voice on human-centered AI.
voices.why: Deep technical contributions combined with thoughtful public leadership.

voices.name: Guillaume Lample
voices.bio: Co-founder of Mistral AI. Previously at Meta FAIR, major contributions to open models.
voices.why: Key technical figure behind one of Europe’s most important AI labs.

voices.name: Jim Fan
voices.bio: Works on foundation agents and embodied AI. Clear and high-signal public communicator.
voices.why: Excellent taste and clarity on the agent and robotics frontier.

voices.name: Riley Goodside
voices.bio: Early and influential voice on advanced prompting and practical LLM usage.
voices.why: High practical signal on what actually works when using frontier models.

voices.name: Two Minute Papers (Károly Zsolnai-Fehér)
voices.bio: Makes cutting-edge research papers accessible through short, enthusiastic videos.
voices.why: Excellent pulse on new research with very high accessibility.

voices.name: Laurence Devillers
voices.bio: Leading French voice on AI ethics, affective computing and societal impact.
voices.why: Important academic and public voice on the ethical dimensions of AI in the French ecosystem.

voices.name: Zvi Mowshowitz
voices.bio: Produces detailed, high-effort analysis of AI developments and risk.
voices.why: Unusually thorough and independent analysis of the AI landscape.

voices.name: Jack Clark
voices.bio: Co-founder of Anthropic and author of the long-running Import AI newsletter. Sharp observer of the industry and policy landscape.
voices.why: One of the best-informed and most consistent analysts of the AI industry trajectory.

voices.name: Helen Toner
voices.bio: Former OpenAI board member. Works on AI policy and governance with strong technical grounding.
voices.why: Rare combination of policy expertise and direct frontier lab experience.

voices.name: Sam Charrington
voices.bio: Long-running technical AI podcast with high-quality interviews of researchers and practitioners.
voices.why: Consistent technical depth over many years.

voices.name: Sarah Guo
voices.bio: Investor and co-host of No Priors. Strong coverage of AI startups and company building.
voices.why: High-signal perspective from the investment and founder side of AI.

voices.name: Elad Gil
voices.bio: Experienced operator and investor. Co-host of No Priors with deep pattern recognition on tech companies.
voices.why: Strong strategic and company-building insights applied to AI.

voices.name: Luc Julia
voices.bio: Well-known French voice on AI, author and public communicator.
voices.why: Accessible and established voice in the French public conversation on AI.

voices.name: Joëlle Pineau
voices.bio: Leading researcher in reinforcement learning and AI systems. Strong academic and industry presence.
voices.why: High technical credibility with clear public communication.

voices.name: Sebastian Raschka
voices.bio: Author and educator focused on practical deep learning and LLMs. Clear technical writing and courses.
voices.why: Excellent practical educational content for builders.

voices.name: Machine Learning Street Talk
voices.bio: In-depth technical and philosophical conversations on machine learning and AI.
voices.why: High-quality long-form research discussions.

voices.name: Hugging Face
voices.bio: Official channel of the Hugging Face ecosystem — models, tools, and open AI education.
voices.why: Central node of the open-source AI community.

voices.name: Ludovic Salenne
voices.bio: Référence francophone sur les outils d’IA générative et les workflows pratiques.
voices.why: Volume et réactivité FR sur les outils du quotidien.

voices.name: The AI Epiphany
voices.bio: Technical deep dives on AI research, agents, and engineering practice.
voices.why: Bonne densité technique, moins de hype.
